title: Outcomes of mandibular reconstruction using conventional plates vs patient-specific implants
html: Recent progress using computer-aided design and computer-aided manufacturing technology has enabled the fabrication of surgical guides and reconstruction plates tailored to individual patients. These patient-specific implants (PSI), which are now being widely used for mandibular reconstruction surgery for oral cancer, have improved the efficiency of surgery and have allowed more precise execution of the preoperative plan. The present study compared the efficacy of PSI with conventional reconstruction plates (CR) requiring bending for mandibular reconstruction following segmental and hemimandibular resection in patients with an oral malignancy who underwent free-flap reconstruction including a reconstruction or bridging plate without bone.
